classification.note: ASan container-overflow WRITE: the AVX2 LSTM kernel writes past std::vector::size() into the reserved-but-unsized capacity of a scratch output buffer. It is an out-of-bounds WRITE (CWE-787); the dataset's primary_category is CWE-125 but the reproduced evidence is a multi-byte WRITE.

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=4759298367422464 Project: tesseract-ocr Fuzzing Engine: libFuzzer Fuzz Target: fuzzer-api Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_tesseract-ocr Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Container-overflow WRITE {*} Crash Address: 0x62100048d47f Crash State: tesseract::ExtractResults16 tesseract::PartialMatrixDotVector16 tesseract::matrixDotVector Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=libfuzzer_asan_tesseract-ocr&range=202103160607:202103170630
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 32142: tesseract has a memory-safety bug. ASan reports a Container-overflow WRITE of size 32 in tesseract::ExtractResults16 <- PartialMatrixDotVector16 <- matrixDotVector, in the AVX2 integer matrix-dot-vector kernel used by the LSTM recognizer. The FullyConnected forward pass allocates its per-timestep output scratch buffer sized to the raw output count no_, while the AVX2 kernel writes Roundup(no_, 8) padded doubles, overrunning the vector's logical size into its reserved capacity when no_ is not a multiple of 8.

source.value_from: Untrusted fuzzer testcase bytes, read bit-by-bit via BitReader BR(data, size) and materialized into a fixed WIDTHxHEIGHT 1-bit Leptonica Pix image; that image is then handed to TessBaseAPI::SetImage/GetUTF8Text and OCR'd, driving the LSTM recognizer whose FullyConnected forward pass reaches the overflowing AVX2 kernel.
source.description: Project-level input materialization: the attacker-controlled fuzzer bytes are decoded into the Pix image that is recognized. This is the concrete load point for the untrusted artifact (as opposed to the LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput harness entry).

tainted_value_origin.description: First vulnerability-relevant materialization inside tesseract proper: the untrusted Pix is converted into the int8 network input tensor `inputs` (int_mode) that is fed to network_->Forward and, per timestep, becomes the `u`/`i_input` operand of WeightMatrix::MatrixDotVector -> the AVX2 kernel that computes the results written into the undersized output buffer.
tainted_value_origin.note: The overflow count itself (Roundup(no_,8) vs no_) is fixed by the network geometry; the untrusted input selects/drives the LSTM path that runs the AVX2 kernel with an output layer whose no_ is not a multiple of 8.

sink.description: 32-byte AVX2 store of 4 doubles into the output vector `v` (the FullyConnected temp_line scratch buffer). ExtractResults16 unconditionally writes 16 doubles per call; across the padded output range the store lands at offset v+12..v+15 which is beyond the vector's logical size() (no_) although still inside its reserved capacity -> ASan container-overflow WRITE at intsimdmatrixavx2.cpp:136.

root_cause.description: The per-thread output scratch buffer is initialized with size = no_ (raw output count) and reserve/capacity = ro = RoundOutputs(no_) (padded to the AVX2 register granularity). FloatVec::Init does vec_->reserve(ro); vec_->resize(no_), so the vector's logical size() is only no_. But when IntSimdMatrix::intSimdMatrix is set, matrixDotVector writes rounded_num_out = Roundup(no_, kNumOutputsPerRegister=8) doubles into the buffer. If no_ is not a multiple of 8, the SIMD kernel stores at indices [no_, rounded_num_out), which are inside the reserved capacity but past size() -> container-overflow WRITE. The fix changes this call to temp_lines[i].Init(ro, scratch), sizing (resize) the buffer to the padded count ro so every SIMD write is within size().

parser_admitted.note: The image has been admitted through the OCR pipeline (GetUTF8Text -> recog_all_words -> classify_word_pass1 -> LSTMRecognizeWord) and the prepared int8 input tensor is now entering the LSTM network forward pass, which dispatches into Series::Forward -> FullyConnected::Forward and the AVX2 matrixDotVector kernel. Earlier than root cause/sink, later than program entry.

coarse_trace.summary: Untrusted fuzzer bytes are decoded via BitReader into a 1-bit Pix image and passed to TessBaseAPI::SetImage/GetUTF8Text for OCR.
Recognition entry point; runs recog_all_words -> classify_word_pass1 which invokes the LSTM recognizer on each word.
Prepares the int8 input tensor from the Pix and calls network_->Forward, entering the LSTM network graph (Series -> FullyConnected).
Allocates the per-timestep output scratch buffer temp_lines[i] with size no_ but reserve ro (=RoundOutputs(no_)); the buffer is undersized for the padded AVX2 write count.
Passes the undersized output_line together with the int8 input line to weights_.MatrixDotVector.
Dispatches to intSimdMatrix->matrixDotVectorFunction (the AVX2 kernel) with dim1=num_out and v = the output buffer.
Computes rounded_num_out = Roundup(num_out, 8) and calls the Partial* kernels writing rounded_num_out doubles into v.
Invokes ExtractResults16 to store the 16 accumulated results into v.
AVX2 32-byte store _mm256_storeu_pd(v + 12, ...) overruns the vector's logical size() into reserved capacity -> container-overflow WRITE.

fine_trace.note: Untrusted fuzzer bytes (BitReader over data,size) are written into the 1-bit Pix image, the attacker-controlled artifact that is subsequently OCR'd via SetImage/GetUTF8Text.
The Pix image is materialized into the int8 network input tensor `inputs` (int_mode) consumed by the LSTM forward pass.
Enters the network graph; Series::Forward -> FullyConnected::Forward runs the vulnerable output-buffer sizing and the AVX2 kernel.

ro is the AVX2 output count rounded up from no_ to the register granularity (multiple of kNumOutputsPerRegister=8); ro >= no_ and equals the number of doubles the SIMD kernel will actually write. This branch is taken because the AVX2 IntSimdMatrix is registered.

Root cause: the output scratch buffer is sized to no_ (via resize) while only its capacity is ro. It should be sized to ro. The patch changes this to Init(ro, scratch). Mark: unsafe sizing of the SIMD output buffer.

size == no_ here, so the vector's logical size() (the ASan container-annotated valid region) is only no_ doubles, even though the preceding vec_->reserve(reserve==ro) at networkscratch.h:147 leaves capacity >= ro. Indices [no_, ro) are reserved-but-poisoned.
The undersized temp_line (output_line, size no_) and the image-derived int8 input line i_input are handed to the weight-matrix multiply that computes the padded results.
Indirect dispatch to the AVX2 matrixDotVector with v = output_line (the undersized buffer) and dim1 = num_out (== no_). Taken because IntSimdMatrix::intSimdMatrix is non-null.
The number of doubles actually written into v is rounded_num_out = Roundup(no_, 8) = ro, which exceeds the buffer's logical size no_ whenever no_ is not a multiple of 8.
Selected for the trailing 16-output group; writes 16 doubles into v at the current output offset.
Stores the 16 accumulated results into v via two ExtractResults16 half-writes.

32-byte AVX2 store lands at v+12..v+15. Across the padded output range these indices reach [no_, rounded_num_out), which is past the vector's size() (no_) but within reserved capacity -> ASan container-overflow WRITE of size 32 at intsimdmatrixavx2.cpp:136. Missing guard: the output buffer was never sized (resized) to the padded write count.

sanitizer_ground_truth.region: 0x62100000b87f is located 895 bytes inside of 4096-byte region [0x62100000b500,0x62100000c500)

cross_validation.note: Sink node (intsimdmatrixavx2.cpp:136 ExtractResults16) is exactly the ASan crash frame 0. coarse_trace/fine_trace call chain matches the reported crash stack ExtractResults16 <- PartialMatrixDotVector16 <- matrixDotVector <- MatrixDotVector <- ForwardTimeStep <- Forward. The container annotation (size) that makes the write out-of-bounds is set by the root-cause Init at fullyconnected.cpp:138; the overflowed region is the reused NetworkScratch FloatVec whose backing store was reserved via networkscratch.h:147.

format.name: tesseract fuzzer-api input (bit-packed 1-bit Pix image)
format.contract: The input is consumed by the tesseract `fuzzer-api` target: its bits are read via BitReader to fill a fixed WIDTHxHEIGHT 1-bit Leptonica Pix, which is OCR'd by TessBaseAPI::GetUTF8Text. To be reachability-comparable a candidate must be admitted through the OCR pipeline far enough to run the LSTM recognizer on at least one word/line (classify_word_pass1 -> LSTMRecognizeWord -> RecognizeLine -> network Forward) so that a FullyConnected layer runs the AVX2 IntSimdMatrix matrixDotVector kernel with an output count no_ that is not a multiple of kNumOutputsPerRegister (8); the kernel then writes Roundup(no_,8) doubles into the temp_line scratch buffer sized only to no_, producing the container-overflow WRITE at intsimdmatrixavx2.cpp:136. The AVX2 path (and thus the padded write) requires the built-in/traineddata network geometry present in the fuzzer image. Original PoC bytes and any target-specific exploit recipe are intentionally excluded.
